explanation: Matches erdosproblems.com/470, second question: 'Are there infinitely many primitive weird numbers, i.e. those such that no proper divisor of n is weird?' The Lean statement asserts the set {n | Nat.Weird n ∧ ∀ d ∈ properDivisors n, ¬ Nat.Weird d} is infinite. Mathlib's Nat.Weird is Abundant (sum of proper divisors > n, i.e. σ(n) > 2n) and not Pseudoperfect; the page's 'σ(n) ≥ 2n' differs only for perfect numbers, which are pseudoperfect and hence never weird, so the notions coincide. Faithful (positive form of the yes/no question).
